summary: Same 24-state cyclic CA with a byte-identical palette and a perfectly matching Speed dial, but the port dies to a solid dark-red grid and hard-reseeds every ~4.4 s instead of the original's ~10.0 s wall-clock reset, its Lifetime dial is inert, and its second Mode draws 5 states (including a navy blue) where the original draws 3.
observations: Both sides render on the default 16x16 grid rig with no compile or runtime errors, no sensor bindings, and the same three sliders (sliderSpeed, sliderLifetime, sliderMode, all kind=slider) - control surfaces match exactly.

CA generation rate matches: at untouched defaults both step 10 generations/s (orig 10.00, port 9.80 non-zero-motion frames per second over 60 s at 20 fps), and the settled state's full 24-colour cycle autocorrelates at 2.40 s on both sides (label late-lt0).

TEMPORAL RHYTHM IS THE BIG DIVERGENCE. Original: a hard whole-grid re-randomization every 10.05 s, dead regular (motion-series autocorrelation peaks at 10.05 s with harmonics at 20.1/30.6/40.8 s; events measured at 10.05, 20.1, 34.85, 44.9, 54.95 s). Port: an equivalent re-randomization every 4.40 s (autocorr peak 4.40 s), i.e. ~2.3x too often.

Between resets the two look qualitatively different at defaults. Original: within ~3 s of a reset the whole grid organizes into a smooth full-coverage phase gradient - a --dump histogram shows all 24 states present at ~10-11% each and 0% of adjacent cell pairs sharing a colour. Port: the grid instead COLLAPSES to a single state - 80-99% of the 256 pixels are 127,0,0 (dark red) at t=3.3, 4.3, 8.3, 13.3, 17.3, 21.3, 25.3, 29.3 s in the same 30 s window - sits frozen there (motion 0-1) for ~0.5 s, then re-randomizes in one frame (filmstrip label reseed-cmp: solid red at 13.35/13.40/13.45/13.50 s, full speckle at 13.55 s, while the original at the same moment is a smooth rainbow gradient gliding steadily).

Consequence for colour: over 240 s untouched the port's mean green is 58.1 vs the original's 74.6 and mean red 84.2 vs 80.3 - not a palette difference (palettes are identical) but a by-product of the port spending far more time in the all-dark-red collapsed state.

CONVERGENCE TO THE ORDERED STATE IS ~5x SLOWER ON THE PORT. With sliderLifetime=0 (reset disabled), sliderSpeed=0.25, sliderMode=0 over 180 s, the original reaches the smooth spiral/gradient attractor by ~16 s and holds it for the remaining 164 s; the port thrashes between speckle and all-red collapse until ~81 s before settling. Once both are settled the pictures are very close in character (label late-lt0, t=150-180 s: both smooth rainbow phase gradients, both meanBrightness ~63, both motion avg 9).

SECOND MODE DIVERGES STRUCTURALLY. At sliderMode=1 the original draws exactly 3 states - 127,0,0 dark red / 0,237,0 green / 0,0,17 near-black (evenly spaced entries of the same 24-colour ramp) - in large clean rounded domains and spiral arms that sweep continuously (motion avg 11.8, only 4 zero-motion frames in 1200 over 120 s, meanB avg 5.6 max 17, i.e. essentially no blue). The port draws 5 states - 127,0,0 / 199,248,0 / 0,202,80 / 0,21,52 (navy) / 4,0,6 - in a speckly texture that repeatedly parks in a near-uniform NAVY BLUE grid for seconds at a time (motion avg 4.5, 94 zero-motion frames, meanB avg 28.7 max 79). The navy state does not exist anywhere in the original's output.

The Mode switch threshold also differs: sweeping 0 to 1 in 0.1 steps, the original flips from the 24-state mode to the 3-state mode between 0.5 and 0.6; the port flips between 0.4 and 0.5. Both dials are 2-position, no third mode on either side.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING. The original's reset interval is wall-clock and fps-invariant: 10.2 s at 5 fps, 10.10 s at 10 fps, 10.05 s at 20 fps, 10.05 s at 40 fps. The port's is generation-counted (~44 generations): 4.40 s at 10/20/40 fps (where the CA is capped at 10 gen/s) but 8.8 s at 5 fps, where the generation rate falls to 5/s. The port's cadence is also completely seed-independent (4.40 s at seeds 1, 7 and 1234) while the original's event train shifts with seed.

Engine-gap aside (not a port fidelity issue): on a --grid 48x48 override the ORIGINAL fails with 'execution limit exceeded (infinite loop?)' at frame 0 while the port renders fine. Both render normally at 8x8 and at the default 16x16.
Untouched-default and explicitly-dialed comparisons agree - untouched defaults land in the 24-state mode on both sides, and every divergence above reproduces with controls explicitly set.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Inverted speed: sets the CA generation rate. Measured non-zero-motion frames/s over 30 s at 20 fps: 0 -> 19.9 gen/s, 0.25 -> 9.9, 0.5 -> 3.3, 0.75 -> 1.7, 1 -> 1.0. Untouched default is 10.0 gen/s.
dials.portEffect: Same inverted mapping, same magnitudes: 0 -> 19.3 gen/s, 0.25 -> 9.6, 0.5 -> 3.9, 0.75 -> 1.6, 1 -> 1.0; default 9.8 gen/s. Only nit is ~16% fast at 0.5 (3.9 vs 3.3).

dials.name: sliderLifetime
dials.origEffect: Sets the period of the whole-grid re-randomization, linearly. Measured by autocorrelation of the motion series over 180 s at 5 fps (speed=0.25, mode=0 pinned): 0 -> NEVER resets (max motion 24 over 180 s, pattern settles into the spiral attractor and stays), 0.25 -> 7.6 s, 0.5 -> 15.2 s, 0.75 -> 22.6 s, 1 -> 30.2 s. Untouched default behaves as ~10.05 s.
dials.portEffect: Effectively inert on the reset cadence. Over the same 180 s sweep the port's dominant period stays ~8.8 s at every setting (0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1); re-checked at 20 fps over 80 s with only Lifetime set, the port's autocorrelation peak is 4.40 s at BOTH Lifetime=0 and Lifetime=1, and at Lifetime=0 it still re-randomizes repeatedly where the original never does. Setting the dial does perturb the run slightly (peak motion 41 vs 69) but does not change the cadence. Verified over multi-event windows (180 s and 240 s), not just the 4 s probe.

dials.name: sliderMode
dials.origEffect: Two-position switch, flipping between 0.5 and 0.6. Low = 24-state rainbow cyclic CA; high = 3-state CA (dark red / green / near-black) with large clean domains and spiral arms, continuously active (motion avg 11.8, 4/1200 zero-motion frames, no blue at all).
dials.portEffect: Two-position switch, but flipping between 0.4 and 0.5. Low mode matches the original's 24-state mode exactly (identical palette). High mode is a 5-state CA including a navy blue (0,21,52) the original never emits; it is speckly rather than domain-forming and repeatedly parks in a near-uniform navy grid (motion avg 4.5, 94/1200 zero-motion frames, meanB 28.7 vs orig 5.6).

feedback: Biggest fix: the port's grid dies to a single state and re-randomizes every ~4.4 s at default dials, where the original re-randomizes every 10.05 s and in between holds a smooth full-coverage phase gradient (all 24 states present at ~10% each, zero adjacent cells sharing a colour). Target the original's default cadence of one hard whole-grid reseed per 10.05 s.

Wire up sliderLifetime. On the original it linearly sets that reseed period: 0 = never reseed at all, 0.25 = 7.6 s, 0.5 = 15.2 s, 0.75 = 22.6 s, 1 = 30.2 s (so roughly 30.2 s x value, with 0 meaning 'off'). On the port the visible cadence is identical at Lifetime 0 and Lifetime 1, and Lifetime=0 does not give a reset-free run.

Make the reset a WALL-CLOCK timer, not a generation counter. The original's period is 10.05 s at 10, 20 and 40 fps and 10.2 s at 5 fps; the port's is 4.40 s at 10/20/40 fps but stretches to 8.8 s at 5 fps, which is the signature of counting CA steps instead of elapsed seconds.

The port's CA is far more prone to collapsing to state 0 (dark red) and far slower to organize. With resets disabled the original reaches the smooth spiral attractor in ~16 s and never leaves; the port needs ~81 s and collapses to >95% dark red repeatedly on the way. Once settled the two look nearly identical, so the ordered-state dynamics are right - it is the neighbour-count / advance rule that is letting the grid die. Aim for the original's behaviour of never collapsing below ~50% single-colour occupancy once organized.

sliderMode's high position should produce THREE states, not five: exactly 127,0,0 / 0,237,0 / 0,0,17 (three evenly spaced entries of the shared 24-colour ramp). The port emits five continuously-sampled colours including a navy 0,21,52 that never appears in the original at any Mode setting, and its high mode is nearly 3x less active (motion avg 4.5 vs 11.8) with long near-frozen navy stretches; the original's high mode is continuously sweeping green/red/black domains.
Move the Mode switch threshold: the original flips modes between 0.5 and 0.6, the port between 0.4 and 0.5, so a user at Mode=0.5 sees the rainbow CA on the original and the few-state CA on the port.
Nothing to change in the palette or the Speed dial - the 24 RGB values are byte-identical and the generation rate tracks the original within a few percent across the whole Speed sweep.
